ash: Quick q — when do we increment patch vs minor for runtime compatibility tweaks? Example: changing KV cache eviction that might slightly alter outputs but doesn't change the API surface. Do we do patch (x.y.z -> x.y.(z+1)) or bump minor? cc @taylor @kai

taylor: My vote: patch if the public contract (HTTP/SDK surface, JSON shapes, function signatures) is unchanged. If behavior changes are observable by downstream users (ordering, tokenization differences, scoring) then minor. Always call it out in release notes. :thinking:

kai: Agree on the contract rule. But note: perf/quantization/runtime optimizations often change outputs in subtle ways. We've shipped those as patches historically to avoid semver churn. Maybe we need an explicit "observable-output" bucket.

dinesh: FWIW we had a rollback once where a quant change changed rerank results and broke an A/B. That was shipped as a patch and it caused customer confusion. I'm leaning conservative: bump minor for any potential user-facing output delta.

maria: Suggestion: make a short rubric in docs: "behaviorally compatible" -> patch; "observably different" -> minor. Include concrete examples (kv cache policy, quantization level changes, prompt pre/post-processing tweaks). Also add an internal tag strategy (buildmeta or prerelease) for internal variants.

ash: For tagging conventions, do we prefer `+buildmeta` (e.g., `1.12.3+kv-evict1`) or prerelease (`1.12.3-kv1`)? Buildmeta is semver compliant but some toolchains drop it. We need something deterministic for rollout/dedup logic.

taylor: Buildmeta is semver legal but many package managers ignore it. If we rely on tag parsing server-side, either works. For customer-facing pins I'd avoid buildmeta-only identifiers. Pre-release is more visible.

release-bot: Deploy queued for v1.12.3-kv1 -> canary (sha: abcdef) :robot_face:

kai: If we use prerelease tags for internal canaries, make sure enterprise/dedicated customers get stable pins (no prerelease) unless they explicitly opt-in. Document that in Dedicated onboarding.

dinesh: Also update the release notes checklist: always include a short "compatibility impact" line and examples of what to test. Pinning guidance in docs: "pin to exact patch to avoid surprises".

maria: I'll draft the policy + a release-note template with examples and a few sample sentences we can copy: e.g., `Behavioral impact: none (patch).` or `Behavioral impact: ordering changed — bumped minor.` Will open PR to docs repo today.

taylor: SGTM. I'll add a semver decision checkbox to the release checklist and a line in the deploy playbook: `If output semantics may change -> bump minor` and require lead sign-off.

ash: +1. Let's aim to merge docs before tomorrow's deploy window (tomorrow 17:00 PT). :hourglass_flowing_sand:
